# Brain Systems

## Canonical Notation & Variables

- Use anatomical directions consistently: anterior/posterior (A/P), superior/inferior (S/I), and left/right (L/R). Define the coordinate convention before using $x,y,z$ for anatomy.
- Use cerebral blood flow (CBF) in $\mathrm{mL\,100\,g^{-1}\,min^{-1}}$, cerebral blood volume (CBV) in $\mathrm{mL\,100\,g^{-1}}$ or fractional change, and $\mathrm{CMRO_2}$ in stated oxygen-consumption units.
- Name cells specifically: excitatory pyramidal neuron, inhibitory interneuron, astrocyte, oligodendrocyte, microglial cell, endothelial cell, pericyte, and vascular smooth-muscle cell.

## Core Scientific Models & Assumptions

- Present gray matter, white matter, CSF, and vasculature as mixed tissue classes at MRI voxel scale, not as cellularly pure compartments. Myelin is produced by oligodendrocytes in the CNS; it affects but is not synonymous with white matter MRI contrast.
- Describe the neurovascular unit as context-dependent cellular and vascular interactions, not a one-cell-to-one-vessel relay. Keep arterial supply, capillary exchange, and venous drainage distinct.
- Do not infer function from gross anatomy alone. Link structure, circuit, measurement modality, and level of inference.

## Terminology Safeguards

Do use: “cortical gray matter,” “subcortical white matter,” “vascular territory,” “pial artery,” “penetrating arteriole,” and “neurovascular unit.”

Don't use: “the brain is wired like a computer,” “glia are support cells” as a complete definition, “capillary dilation” as a generic account of flow control, or “neural tissue” when vascular tissue is included.

## Key Equations & Diagrams

```latex
\mathrm{OEF}=\frac{C_{a\mathrm O_2}-C_{v\mathrm O_2}}{C_{a\mathrm O_2}},
\qquad
\mathrm{CMRO}_2=\mathrm{CBF}\,(C_{a\mathrm O_2}-C_{v\mathrm O_2}).
```

For anatomy diagrams, include orientation markers and distinguish arteries, capillaries, veins, neurons, and glia with a legend.
